gates.gate: 1. Idle: inner rings C and D rotate continuously and harmoniously, never rock back and forth
gates.evidence: Fresh 8 s idle on the lane lab (judge2/an/lane_idle8.txt): C turns at a constant 90.00 deg/s and D at 45.00 deg/s about one fixed axis, with 0 reversals and 0 deg wobble. The BASE build (?spin=f2, judge2/an/base_f2_idle8_cd.txt) reversed C 4 times and D 16 times, with D swinging between 1.2 and 113 deg/s (the rocking the user saw). Looked at C and D alone every 0.2 s: judge2/eyes/lane_cd_idle_every02.jpg shows each ring turning over through edge-on; judge2/eyes/base_cd_idle_every02.jpg shows both folding back near face-on.

gates.gate: 1b. Idle C and D match Default Loop.mp4
gates.evidence: Blurred luminance distance to all 121 loop frames (judge2/an/structcmp_lane_vs_base.txt): the lane is closer than BASE in 105/121 frames and in 30/30 of the frames where the two differ most. In the 16 frames where BASE scores closer (margin at most 0.012), lane and BASE look the same and both match (judge2/eyes/idle_base_better_frames.jpg). Sheets compared every 0.2 s: judge2/eyes/ref_loop_inner_every02.jpg vs judge2/eyes/lane_idle_inner_every02.jpg. Video: judge2/vid/idle_lane_left_ref_right_8s.mp4.

gates.gate: 2. Hold: C and D keep turning in slow motion, never reversing
gates.evidence: In every hold, C slows from -90 to -18 deg/s and D from +45 to +9 deg/s with 0 reversals. Runs covered: press at tau 0, 1.3, 2.6 and 3.3 with 10 s holds, a 20 s hold, a re-press 0.35 s after release, and short presses (judge2/an/lane_*.txt). The largest change per tick is 3.05 deg/s for C and 1.53 for D. BASE reversed C 5 times and D 6 times. Looked at the isolated view judge2/eyes/lane_cd_hold_t26.jpg.

gates.gate: 3. Hold: A's quarters and B's halves stay aligned, coplanar, and turn as one ring while split
gates.evidence: Every piece has exactly its ring's rotation (0.00 deg) and sits at most 3.2e-5 m off the ring plane. Offset direction error is at most 0.28 deg, and the four quarters move out by equal amounts (within 2.4e-5 m). A's opening is 0.362 m at F372, 0.570 at F420, and a constant 0.600 m from F436 to release, with share 1.00 at all 5 press moments and in the 20 s hold (judge2/an/*_aclose.txt), so it no longer pulses. BASE pushed pieces up to 0.499 m out of plane, with 0.40 m difference between quarters. Looked at judge2/eyes/lane_tick360_fullres.jpg, lane_h10_t26_sustain_every40.jpg and hold_t26_vs_ref_1/2.jpg.

gates.gate: 4. Hold: the small crystals slow down like the reference
gates.evidence: Crystal speed goes from 1 to 0.50 of idle and back, changing at most 0.021 per tick. They slow over F358-F376 and recover over F449-F467 after release, which are the reference's windows. Zoom-independent speed (speed / sqrt(area)): the reference drops from 0.962 at idle to 0.694 in the hold (x0.72); the lane drops from 1.101 to 0.729 (x0.66) (judge2/an/ref_sbig.txt, lane_idle_sbig.txt, lane_h10_t26_svnorm.txt). BASE only slowed to 0.93. The big-crystal speed and swarm shape are covered by the second minor finding.

gates.gate: 5. Seamless from rest through press, any hold length, release and re-press; a click does nothing
gates.evidence: Holds of 0.3, 0.7, 1.2, 2, 4, 6, 10 and 20 s, plus a re-press 0.35 s after release. Largest change of angular velocity per tick: A 8.4 deg/s (its own idle precession, also present at rest), B 6.2, C 3.05, D 1.53. Ring clock changes at most 0.034 per tick and holds at 0.724 through the re-press click window before easing. Opening changes at most 0.079 per tick. Camera moves 5-18 mm per tick at the re-press. No page errors. Looked at judge2/eyes/lane_rp035_release_repress.jpg and lane_press12_seq.jpg; videos in judge2/vid/. A 0.15 s click: no opening, no zoom, speed unchanged (spreadA 0, camExpand 0, spin 1). With the pointer at three screen corners the rings stay in frame (judge2/eyes/edge_pointer_holds.jpg).

Minor 1: the hold is framed at 0.84x the reference's scale. Minor 2: the nearest crystals move 1.4x faster than the reference's and the swarm's outer edge sits 15% wider. Nits: the rotating hold does not reproduce the reference's arrangement, crystals are bigger and fewer, and the camera lunge is fast. See judge2/eyes/ref_F440_vs_lane_tick400_faceon.jpg, hold_t26_vs_ref_2.jpg and crystals_pinned_ref_lane_main.jpg.

Lane ?spin=f2 vs judge1's BASE captures (idle8, h10_t26): ring orientations and drivers identical; pieces differ by 0.3 mm (capture-tool camera timing). The diff map judge2/eyes/diffmap_hf_vs_main__lane_vs_main_F420.jpg shows only water-ripple timing noise for hf vs MAIN, and only the crystals for lane vs MAIN.

Lane vs MAIN: idle rings and camera identical from tick 1. T0 and T2 render rest, hold and release with no page errors (judge2/eyes/tiers_T0_T2_smoke.jpg). Typecheck tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.hero.json exits 0 with no output. findings.title: The hold zooms in only 0.84x as far as the reference (lead hotfix CameraRig.frameShare / holdShare)
findings.evidence: In the hold the camera stays 14.91-15.11 m from the orb, giving 112-113 px/m at the orb (judge2/an/lane_h10_t26_cam.txt, fov 25.54 deg). The reference gives 132-133 px/m (A2 R8: orb 218 px wide; ORB_RADIUS 0.8255 m), and BASE stopped at 13.0 m. The orb centre is in the right place (723,392 vs 720,392). The reference's open frame fills the screen (A2 R4: 805x733 px at F436, top arc at y 0-5, bottom arc at 735-750). The lane's face-on A reaches only about 85-88% of that (radius 336 px vs 372-396 px). Clearly visible side by side: judge2/eyes/ref_F440_vs_lane_tick400_faceon.jpg. On 390x844 portrait the opened arcs are also cut at the left and right edges (judge2/eyes/portrait_390_holds.jpg), which the hotfix accepted as a 21-28 px crop.
findings.fix_hint: On landscape, take the hold dolly all the way to the reference's 133 px/m (holdShare 1) and keep the opening constant. Limit ring A by what the reference itself does: at F436-F444 its arcs touch or clip the top and bottom edges by a few px. Alternatively, let the push grow as in A2 R4 (centre-line x1.14 at F420 to x1.25 at F440, i.e. +0.31 to +0.55 m) so the worst tumble phase clips at most about 20 px. Leave portrait on fitR / holdFit, then re-check H-G2 against that limit.

findings.title: In the hold the nearest crystals move ~1.4x faster on screen than the reference's, and the swarm's outer edge sits 15% wider
findings.evidence: Pinned comparison, identical crystal phases, sustain F376-F442 (judge2/an/pinned_t26_lane_vs_main.txt, pinned_t13_lane_vs_main.txt). Big crystals (area over 800 px) move 23.2 / 22.9 px per frame vs 16.3 in the reference. Distance from the orb at p90 is 550 px vs 477 (p50 400-403 vs 387 matches). Small and mid crystals are at or below the reference (11.8-16.0 vs 17.0-20.8). Fix round 1 improved on MAIN (big 28.0-28.4 px/frame, p90 625-626). Causes: in the 18-crystal swarm the biggest crystals are simply the nearest ones (pre-existing). In addition, the depth widening is symmetric (shardOutB z +30%, shardOutA z +20%), so it also pulls each belt's front crystals 0.6-1.2 m toward the camera, about 6-11% bigger and faster on screen. Only the crystals behind the orb need the extra room. Looked at judge2/eyes/crystals_pinned_ref_lane_main.jpg and crystal_motion_consecutive.jpg.
findings.fix_hint: Widen the belts in depth only behind the belt origin, for example in SHARD_VERT: cen.z *= 1.0 + uOut[orbit].z * (1.0 - smoothstep(-0.5, 0.0, cen.z)) (+z points toward the camera; this stays smooth across z = 0). Keep the across-view shares. Then re-measure per size class with judge2/tools/sbig.py (target 16-21 px/frame) and the p90 distance with srad.py, both pinned, and re-run the crystal-vs-opened-piece capsule test. Whatever excess remains belongs to the crystal owner (crystal sizes and nearness).

findings.title: Camera lunge too fast, and the creep starts by backing off (pre-existing hold-lane camera curve)

summary:
Rings lane, judge round 2: FAIL, lens 7.8. There is no blocker and no major finding; two minor findings and four nits remain. Everything below comes from fresh captures made through the slot on the lane lab (:5174), compared with MAIN (:5173), BASE behaviour (?spin=f2) and the reference frames.

Everything the user complained about in this lens is fixed and measured exact:
- Idle: C and D now turn continuously at 90 and 45 deg/s, never reversing (BASE reversed them 4 and 16 times). The idle is closer to Default Loop than BASE in 105 of 121 frames.
- Hold: C and D slow to -18 and +9 deg/s, still never reversing.
- Split rings: A's quarters and B's halves keep their ring's exact rotation and plane. The opening holds at a constant 0.6 m with no pulse, at every press moment and in a 20 s hold.
- Crystals: they slow to 0.5 of idle with the reference's timing (F358-F376, back over F449-F467).
- Seamless: press, holds from 0.3 s to 20 s, release and a re-press 0.35 s later are all continuous, and a click does nothing.
- No regressions: ?spin=f2 restores BASE exactly and ?spin=hf restores MAIN exactly. T0 and T2 render with no errors, and the typecheck passes.

What keeps it from passing:
- Minor 1: the hold zooms in only 0.84x as far as the reference (112 vs 133 px/m at the orb). This comes from the lead's hotfix, which stops the camera early so ring A stays inside the frame.
- Minor 2: in the hold the nearest crystals still move about 1.4x faster on screen than the reference's, and the swarm's outer edge sits 15% wider. Fix round 1 made both better than MAIN.
- Nits: the rotating hold does not reproduce the reference's arrangement, crystals are bigger and fewer, the camera lunge is fast, and D looks almost still in the hold.
